prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: 中文 · API 参数说明 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "参数" · longest unbreakable word 139px · one-line width 139px
  col 2: header "类型" · longest unbreakable word 56px · one-line width 56px
  col 3: header "必填" · longest unbreakable word 18px · one-line width 35px
  col 4: header "默认值" · longest unbreakable word 93px · one-line width 93px
  col 5: header "说明" · longest unbreakable word 110px · one-line width 552px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 624px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 623px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Identifiers and defaults stay intact, and the description has reasonable space, but the 必填 header wraps and HTTPS 协议 is split across lines."},"B":{"grade":"good","why":"Headers and identifiers remain intact, but extra width in the parameter column leaves descriptions narrow and produces several short lines."},"C":{"grade":"excellent","why":"All headers and identifiers stay intact, while the description column has enough room for a clear, balanced reading rhythm."},"D":{"grade":"bad","why":"Equal-looking columns waste space in the short fields, split parameter identifiers, and squeeze descriptions into many short lines."},"E":{"grade":"good","why":"Headers and identifiers stay intact, but the narrow description column makes several rows taller and leaves short final lines."},"F":{"grade":"good","why":"The wide description column reads comfortably and identifiers stay intact, but the 必填 header wraps vertically, weakening the header hierarchy."}},"best":["C"],"confidence":"high","unsure":"C and F are close: F gives descriptions more room, but C keeps every header on one line."}
